intro: When you search for a party wall surveyor near me, you likely need someone local who can help with a notice or a party wall agreement under the Party Wall etc. Act. Whether you are the owner doing the work or the neighbour affected, you want clear guidance on the next steps and a surveyor who can act fairly. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with no obligation.
need_heading: What people searching for a party wall surveyor usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a party wall surveyor are dealing with a specific building project or a notice they have received.
needs: You are planning work such as a loft conversion, extension or basement and have been told you need to serve a party wall notice on your neighbour.
You have received a party wall notice from a neighbour and want to understand your rights and what happens next.
You and your neighbour have agreed to use a single surveyor to prepare a party wall agreement and need someone to act for both of you.
You are buying or selling a property and need a party wall agreement or schedule of condition to clarify the state of a shared wall.
You need a surveyor who can act impartially and prepare a party wall agreement that protects both sides if there is a dispute.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about party wall matters
context: The Party Wall etc. Act sets out the process for work that affects shared walls, boundaries or nearby foundations. Notices must be served before work starts, and if you and your neighbour cannot agree, you each appoint a surveyor or agree on a single surveyor to make a party wall agreement.

A party wall agreement is a legally binding document that sets out how the work should be carried out and protects both parties. Many party wall surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and some belong to the Faculty of Party Wall Surveyors. You can check a surveyor's membership and ask about their experience with the Act.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of work you are planning or the notice you have received, including whether it is for a loft conversion, extension, basement or other structural change.
Say whether you are the building owner or the adjoining owner, as this affects what the surveyor will do for you.
Mention if you have already spoken to your neighbour and whether they are likely to agree to a single surveyor.
Give the location of the property so we can introduce you to a surveyor who works in your area.
State whether you need a full party wall agreement or just a schedule of condition.
Include any deadlines you are aware of, such as the notice period, so the surveyor can prioritise your enquiry.
questions: Are you a member of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors or the Faculty of Party Wall Surveyors?
Have you handled many party wall matters for projects like mine?
Will you act as a single surveyor for both parties or would you represent only me?
What is your process for serving notices and preparing a party wall agreement?
How do you handle disagreements between neighbours during the process?
What are your fees and what do they cover?

faqs.q: Do I always need a party wall surveyor?
faqs.a: Not always. If the work is minor and your neighbour agrees in writing, you may not need a surveyor. However, for work covered by the Party Wall etc. Act, such as loft conversions or extensions, a surveyor is often needed to prepare a party wall agreement if there is no agreement.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a party wall agreement and a schedule of condition?
faqs.a: A party wall agreement is a legal document that resolves a dispute and sets out how the work will be carried out. A schedule of condition is a record of the condition of a neighbouring property before work starts, often used to protect against later claims of damage.

faqs.q: Can my neighbour and I use the same surveyor?
faqs.a: Yes, if you both agree, you can appoint a single surveyor to act impartially for both parties. This is often simpler and less expensive than each appointing your own surveyor.

faqs.q: How do I find a party wall surveyor near me?
faqs.a: You can search for surveyors in your area through the RICS directory or ask for recommendations. iComply can also introduce you to a suitable local surveyor who will quote you directly.
